notes.author: Mira Castellanos
notes.text: Kickoff with Gunnar Halvorsen and Deb Okafor. Mandate: replace the 1990s core ledger with the new cloud core by Q4. Board approved $4.2M for our part plus $11M vendor budget. Gunnar wants a single cutover weekend: "one weekend, one pain, done."

notes.author: Arjun Mehta
notes.text: Interface discovery found 212 point-to-point integrations off the old core (card processor, ATM switch, loan origination, three regulatory feeds). Only 140 were documented. Flagged to Paul Lindqvist as the biggest cutover risk.

notes.author: Mira Castellanos
notes.text: Big-bang cutover rehearsal #1 failed at hour 19: ATM switch reconciliation mismatch of $1.37M in test balances, rollback took 9 hours. Deb Okafor: "If this happens live, we are on the front page."

notes.author: Arjun Mehta
notes.text: Rehearsal #2 also failed. Loan origination system could not read new account numbers; 38 undocumented batch jobs still pointed at the old ledger. Team morale low; vendor blaming our interface inventory.

notes.author: Mira Castellanos
notes.text: Steering committee agreed to abandon big-bang. New plan: migrate by product line (savings first, then deposits, cards, loans) with a 6-week parallel run for each wave and a reconciliation dashboard owned by finance.

notes.author: Arjun Mehta
notes.text: Wave 1 (savings, ~310k accounts) went live. Parallel run caught 2 rounding differences in interest accrual before customers saw them. Zero customer-facing incidents.

notes.author: Arjun Mehta
notes.text: Waves 2 and 3 complete. Each wave's go/no-go now gated on a green reconciliation dashboard for 10 consecutive business days. Paul says the gate is the reason the business trusts the program again.

notes.author: Mira Castellanos
notes.text: Loans wave live; old core decommissioned. Program finished 7 weeks later than the original big-bang date but with no customer-facing outage. Gunnar in close-out: "We should have started phased." Engagement closed.

simulation.lesson: For large core-platform migrations with many poorly documented downstream integrations, a phased rollout by business line, with a parallel-run period and an objective reconciliation gate before each wave, succeeds where a single all-at-once cutover repeatedly fails. The underlying cause of failure is hidden integration dependencies that only surface under real load; phasing limits the blast radius and lets each wave expose them safely.
simulation.why: Hidden integration dependencies surface under real load; phasing plus a reconciliation gate contains the damage and rebuilds stakeholder trust.
simulation.conditions: Many downstream integrations, incomplete interface documentation, high cost of customer-facing failure.
